catch_up.description: What changed in mail, calendar and contacts since a point in time.
catch_up.text:
Tell me what changed since 24h.
Use outlook_changes_since(fallback_window_hours=...) — it composes the mail, calendar and contacts delta queries into one digest and hands back per-resource delta tokens. Keep those tokens and pass them back next time; that call then returns only what changed, which is roughly ten times cheaper than re-scanning.
Summarise: new mail worth my attention (it flags high-importance and flagged items for you), calendar changes, and anything cancelled.
catch_up.title: Catch up since

morning_brief.description: Today's calendar, unread mail and tasks due, in one pass.
morning_brief.text:
Give me a brief for today, in this order:
1. outlook_list_events(days=1, concise=True) — what is scheduled.
2. outlook_list_inbox(folder='inbox', unread_only=True, concise=True, count=25) — what arrived and is unread.
3. outlook_list_tasks() — what is due.
Then summarise in plain language: what is on, what needs a reply, what is overdue. Lead with anything time-critical. Do not open individual messages unless the preview is genuinely ambiguous — and if you need several, use outlook_read_messages once rather than outlook_read_message in a loop.
morning_brief.title: Morning brief

triage_folder.description: Scan one folder cheaply and act on it in a single batch.
triage_folder.text:
Triage 'inbox':
1. outlook_list_inbox(folder='inbox', count=50, concise=True) — one scan. The folder name goes straight in; there is no need to list folders first.
2. Sort what you find into: needs a reply, read and archive, junk, ignore.
3. Apply the result with outlook_batch_triage in ONE call rather than a mark-read/move/delete per message.
Tell me what you did and what you left for me. Ask before deleting anything you are not confident about — deletes are recoverable from Deleted Items, but replies are not.
triage_folder.title: Triage a folder
